interpretation: All twelve opportunity controls improve validation RankIC over their exact no-opportunity scoring controls. Ranking gains do not establish portfolio gains.
CSI300 static-risk opportunity strength 0.5 increases seed-0 AR from 0.22918 to 0.25831, with slightly higher STD; seed 1 loses AR while seed 2 gains AR.

CSI300 three-seed avg_none opportunity scoring improves AR 0.14788 -> 0.15332, STD 0.17136 -> 0.17048 and MDD -0.15645 -> -0.15533 versus matched static scoring. ICIR and RankICIR decrease slightly. Unpenalized alpha ensemble retains higher AR with higher volatility.

SP500 original-alpha seeds 1/2 expose substantial instability. Independent-regime three-seed avg_none AR is 0.10441 rather than the favorable seed-0 AR 0.22623; the no-penalty three-seed ensemble AR is 0.00615.
SP500 opportunity scoring generally raises volatility and worsens drawdown relative to matched static/regime controls; retain these negative outcomes.
Stronger SP500 penalties lower volatility further but substantially reduce AR. No scheme has been selected using test performance and superiority to all baselines is unproven.
